A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Lotus. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated or renumbered in v5.

before.justification: v4 reports original depth and surface-normal estimation results, component ablations, parameterization experiments, and qualitative applications.

after.justification: v5 retains original geometric prediction experiments and adds semantic segmentation, diffuse reflectance, and further controlled analyses.

M1.justification: v5 adopts disparity-space targets for depth training and prediction (Sections 5.1 and 5.3). Table 3 retains v4's final configurations and adds explicitly labeled disparity-space variants, establishing an actual procedural change. The architecture, single-step formulation, detail preserver, and generative/discriminative variants remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v5 adds DIODE depth evaluation and OASIS normal evaluation to Tables 1–2. Appendix E additionally trains and evaluates semantic segmentation and diffuse reflectance on Hypersim, substantially extending task requirements beyond geometric prediction. The original depth/normal training datasets remain.

E2.justification: Diffusion-E2E-FT is newly included in both depth and normal comparisons in Tables 1–2. The existing comparator membership is otherwise retained. Reusing Direct Adaptation for the new Hypersim tasks does not introduce another comparison method.

E3.justification: The added studies substantially expand evaluation design: Appendix E specifies 500 randomly selected test pairs and mIoU/mAcc or L1/L2 metrics; Appendix B introduces matched AMRN controls; Appendix F uses 100 sampled cases and eight frequency groups; Appendix G varies the single timestep while excluding detail preservation and mixed-dataset training. Existing geometric metrics and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and training-step ablations, v5 adds disparity-target ablations in Table 3, parameterization/single-step/detail-preserver comparisons with and without AMRN in Tables 4–5, frequency analysis of geometry versus texture in Figure 13, and single-timestep sensitivity in Table 8. These test several previously unexamined explanations and conditions.

E5.justification: Tables 6–7 newly state that results are means from 10 independent runs. This adds explicit repeated-run reporting without identifying training versus inference repetitions or supplying dispersion. The original variance-band plots remain; the PDFs do not establish increased repetition of the original experiments.

E6.justification: v5 adds benchmark, comparator, and analysis results and revises Lotus scores. Table 3 retains the earlier Lotus-G KITTI AbsRel of 11.324 and adds 8.521 for disparity-space training, so these are different configurations. Table 2 changes Lotus-D's NYUv2 mean angular error from 16.8 to 16.2 without explaining the revision. New segmentation results include mIoU 21.2 versus Direct Adaptation's 14.1. Updated average ranks use expanded comparison sets.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds limiting-case reasoning for approximate equivalence between v-prediction and x0-prediction at t=T when the noise coefficient's complementary signal term approaches zero. The original numbered diffusion equations and Appendix C derivation are retained; no new theorem or substantial proof framework appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace the assertion of state-of-the-art depth/normal performance with promising performance, narrowing the claimed comparative standing. Section 5.2 specifies Lotus-G's best overall rank. The central formulation, detail-preservation, efficiency, and limited-training-data contributions remain.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly explains that AMRN reduces parameterization differences and can make single-step gains inconsistent, qualifying the original adaptation argument. Appendix F interprets frequency behavior as preserving geometric detail without copying texture, while Appendix E extends the applicability discussion through non-geometric tasks. These substantially expand the paper's explanations and applicability conditions.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly discloses normalization of depth and normal maps to [-1,1]; added analyses identify the Marigold codebase and FFT grouping procedure. Hardware, optimizer, training durations, and access links remain unchanged. Appendix B drops the explicit exclusion of test-time ensembling, a disclosure change that does not establish changed inference.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds substantive positioning against concurrent Diffusion-E2E-FT, acknowledging similar performance and distinguishing Lotus-G's stochastic predictions and detail preserver. References to Garcia et al., Disenvisioner, and DIODE are added. The broader related-work organization and existing comparisons remain.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Changes include localized wording edits, clarification that the autoencoder contains an encoder and decoder, an expanded related-work paragraph, and new appendix subsections. Earlier appendices E–G become H–J without substantial rewriting.

P2.justification: v5 substantially expands visual presentation with Tables 4–8 and Figures 12–13, additional columns and rows in Tables 1–3, and revised Figure 1 comparison charts. The earlier qualitative and application Figures 12–14 are retained as Figures 14–16, with layout reflow rather than new experiments.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially strengthens the central adaptation argument by testing the previously unexamined AMRN interaction and adding a close concurrent comparator. Non-geometric experiments provide measured support for applicability beyond v4's geometric tasks, while headline performance claims become better calibrated. These gains outweigh remaining reporting gaps, including absent dispersion for ten-run means and Appendix A.2's outdated four-dataset descriptions.
